tool_rules.reason: Kimi Code's Anthropic endpoint has no verified execution contract for these provider-owned declarations. CSSwitch drops only the typed forms and recomputes tool_choice; ordinary Python, Bash, Compute, web_search functions and host.mcp orchestration remain client-owned. 开放平台与订阅制编码端点共用一个 contract：证据来自 api.kimi.com/coding 的实测，开放平台按用户判定沿用同一套补偿，未独立实测。

Claude Science sends a non-standard thinking type of `auto`. Live probes against api.kimi.com/coding show the k3 family silently returns no thinking blocks for `auto` (and for `adaptive`), while omitting the field entirely leaves the upstream default thinking on for all four published models. CSSwitch therefore removes only those two non-standard values and passes the standard `enabled`/`disabled` through untouched. Rewriting to `enabled` would also work upstream but would pull in the thinking-continuity store, which this upstream does not need: live multi-turn probes confirm it accepts history whose assistant thinking blocks were stripped, including messages carrying tool_use, so the DeepSeek chain-break defect does not apply here. 开放平台与订阅制编码端点共用一个 contract：证据来自 api.kimi.com/coding 的实测，开放平台按用户判定沿用同一套补偿，未独立实测。

Kimi for Coding rejects `tool_choice: {"type": "tool"}` with 400 `tool_choice 'specified' is incompatible with thinking enabled` whenever thinking is on, and its thinking is on by default, so a request that merely omits the field still fails. A captured Claude Science session reproduces this on every work-item classifier call. CSSwitch keeps the forced tool — the classifier depends on receiving structured output — and sets thinking to disabled for that one request instead. The `any` and `auto` forms are unaffected upstream and are deliberately left alone, unlike the DeepSeek policy which disables thinking for both. 开放平台与订阅制编码端点共用一个 contract：证据来自 api.kimi.com/coding 的实测，开放平台按用户判定沿用同一套补偿，未独立实测。

Kimi for Coding's Anthropic surface does not implement the `document` content block. Live probes show every source form fails identically — base64 application/pdf, text/plain, url, and a bare {"type":"document"} with no source — each returning the opaque `400 invalid_request_error: "Invalid request Error"`. A control block type that does not exist at all returns that same message, which places `document` in the parser's unknown-block path rather than a format mismatch. Because the block persists in conversation history, one attachment fails every later turn of the session. This is the payload of Claude Science's platform PDF-vision path: a captured session shows read_file(pages=[1]) returning tool_result {"status":"queued_for_vision"} followed by a "[System] Attached file" text block and the PDF as a `document` block. That payload is a real PDF rather than a pre-rendered image: media_type application/pdf, 134 KB against a 1.28 MB 21-page file on disk, i.e. the requested pages extracted into a smaller PDF. Rasterising it is the model provider's job — official Anthropic supports PDF document blocks natively — so on this upstream nothing arrives to render. That platform path therefore does not work on this channel, and CSSwitch cannot make it work — it replaces each block with an attributed note naming the media type so the turn survives instead of failing, and points at the route that does work. Reading PDFs is still possible: the agent can render pages locally and pass them as image blocks, which this upstream accepts; a live session read a scanned patent exactly that way. The loss is not a CSSwitch regression relative to sibling channels either — DeepSeek's endpoint accepts the same block but answers CANNOT_READ with or without it, for both a synthetic marker PDF and the real 133 KB patent. Image blocks are untouched. 开放平台与订阅制编码端点共用一个 contract：证据来自 api.kimi.com/coding 的实测，开放平台按用户判定沿用同一套补偿，未独立实测。

tool_rules.reason: DeepSeek documents provider-side code execution and MCP as unsupported or ignored and does not publish stable Web Fetch, tool-search or advisor executors. CSSwitch drops only those typed declarations and recomputes tool_choice instead of accepting a 2xx as fake execution success.
Unknown non-empty typed vendor tools are preserved opaquely for compatibility and produce a rule-only diagnostic. CSSwitch does not claim an executor or rewrite their payloads.
DeepSeek rejects forced tool use combined with thinking, so CSSwitch disables thinking for forced Anthropic tool_choice on DeepSeek.

CSSwitch drops web_search for exact DashScope Responses request shapes while preserving other function tools, for provider compatibility. Behavior is covered by source, fixture, loopback, and release validation.

transport_rules.reason: Anthropic/Claude hosts are fast-failed with 401 so Science treats virtual login as logged out instead of retrying organization switching.

Non-Anthropic CONNECT opens a direct TCP tunnel. One 10-second dial budget starts before synchronous DNS and is shared across resolved addresses; std DNS itself cannot be interrupted by that budget. External MCP access can still fail where direct egress is blocked.
The virtual sandbox intentionally does not set http_proxy because the CSSwitch proxy does not implement ordinary absolute-form HTTP forwarding.
An upstream proxy path is the recommended future fix for external MCP egress, but it is not implemented in the current main branch.
